correctness.rationale: For every fixed symmetric pair, the projected one-dimensional Gaussian transport formula expands uniformly to ε²(uᵀDu)²/4+O(ε³). The uniform angular representation m+r cos(2θ−α) and exact moments E cos²=1/2, E cos⁴=3/8 give orthogonal variance ε⁴r⁴/128+O(ε⁵) and iid variance ε⁴r²(r²+16m²)/256+O(ε⁵). For r>0 their ratio tends to 2r²/(r²+16m²), and strict signs are justified only away from equality. Swapped Gaussian covariance axes make the two projected squared costs exactly identical and nonconstant, attaining the sharp factor two. The standalone verifier passed 1471 checks; finite sampling is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Gaussian squared sliced transport provides a canonical smooth projection-quadrature benchmark. The formula separates covariance scale mismatch from trace-free anisotropy mismatch, identifies a sharp and computable criterion to choose iid or orthogonal directions locally, and establishes exact worst-case variance inflation on nonsingular population Gaussians. This is a natural structural parameter classification, not just a one-off numeric counterexample or the generic factor-two inequality.
